facts.value: Culture and religion have usually been seen as closely related.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Paul Tillich looked at religion as the soul of culture and culture as the form or framework of religion.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Religion as ultimate concern is the meaning-giving substance of culture, and culture is the totality of forms in which the basic concern of religion expresses itself. In abbreviation: religion is the substance of culture, culture is the form of religion.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Ernst Troeltsch looked at culture as the soil of religion and thought that transplanting a religion from its original culture to a foreign culture would kill it.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Domenic Marbaniang has argued that elements grounded on beliefs of a metaphysical nature (religious) are distinct from elements grounded on nature and the natural (cultural).
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Language (with its grammar) is a cultural element while sacralization of language in which a particular religious scripture is written is more often a religious practice.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: The same applies to music and the arts.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA

facts.value: Criticism of religion is criticism of the ideas, the truth, or the practice of religion, including its political and social implications.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies (Religion, Politics and Global Affairs) - BA
